These 20 hypotheses come from reasoning about the search space and prior knowledge of NAS-Bench-201. I did not run any queries against the benchmark data. They rest on three regularities:

- **Ceiling and floor:** an edit gains more when it replaces a weak op (none) and less when the parent is already strong.
- **Redundancy:** removing an edge costs less when a parallel edge into node 3 already carries a conv.
- **Bottleneck:** cutting the last remaining input to node 3 is far more costly than cutting one of several.
